mentions.name: Photo-to-DMC embroidery thread matching tool
mentions.description: This tool turns photos of birds and mountains into embroidery plans: it applies Minecraft-style colour theory to meanshift the image down to a lower colour resolution, matches the reduced palette to DMC threads, fills in gradients, and uses hue shift/temperature changes to represent shadows (e.g. purple as a shaded green rather than a darker green). The author also uses it to explore the Claude Code web setup.
mentions.problem: Figuring out which floss to buy; colour sampling from OKLab space needs to be pulled local because gradient colours are picked out of order instead of projected onto the target line.
mentions.source_excerpt:
the general idea is to take pictures of birds and mountains, and use a bunch of colour-theory-from-minecraft

to first meanshift a bunch of the image to come up with a lower colour resolution image, then to match that to dmc threads
